@graph.articleBody: Distillation is, at bottom, an arbitrage: the capability embedded in a $40M-$500M frontier training run can be harvested through an API for a four- or five-figure query bill and re-trained into a small model for hundreds of dollars. That asymmetry is now visible in published price lists, where the gap between a vendor's flagship and its small tier runs 10x to 42x on output tokens, and in the research record, where Sky-T1-32B was distilled for under $450 and s1-32B for a reported ~$50. It became a macro event on 27 January 2025, when DeepSeek-R1 and its six open-weight distilled students wiped $589B off Nvidia's market capitalisation in a single session - the largest one-day loss in stock-market history - and it became a policy event in February 2026 when OpenAI told the House Select Committee on China that DeepSeek was running obfuscated distillation pipelines against its models. The counter-trend matters too: Epoch AI measures inference prices for a fixed capability level falling 9x-900x per year, which compresses the payback on self-hosting a distilled model to the point where, on our own TCO model, a single-GPU deployment only beats Claude Haiku 4.5 above ~658M output tokens a month and never beats the cheapest serverless open-model endpoints.

@graph.name: The economics of AI distillation: prices, training costs, and the market shocks — glossary

hasDefinedTerm.name: MTok
hasDefinedTerm.description: One million tokens. The standard unit for LLM API pricing. Input and output tokens are billed at different rates, with output typically 4-5x more expensive.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Blended cost per MTok
hasDefinedTerm.description: A single price figure for a workload with a known input:output ratio. For a 4:1 ratio, blended cost per million output tokens = 4 x input price + output price. Used throughout the TCO tables here.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Teacher API cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: The money paid to a frontier vendor for the inference calls that generate a distillation corpus. Usually the dominant cash cost of a distillation project, larger than the student fine-tune itself.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Amortised training cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: Epoch AI's accounting method: hardware depreciation plus energy over the final training run. Produces figures roughly half those of cloud-rental accounting, which charges the full market rate for every chip-hour.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cloud-rental accounting
hasDefinedTerm.description: Costing a training run at the price of renting equivalent GPUs on the open market. Used by the Stanford AI Index. Gives $78M for GPT-4 where Epoch's amortised method gives ~$40M.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Marginal training cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: The GPU-hour bill for a single successful run, excluding R&D, failed runs, data acquisition, staff and infrastructure. DeepSeek's $5.6M and $294,000 figures are both marginal costs.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Provisioned Throughput
hasDefinedTerm.description: AWS Bedrock's committed-capacity billing mode, charged hourly per Model Unit. Custom and distilled models on Bedrock can only be served this way, which imposes a fixed monthly floor regardless of volume.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Prompt caching
hasDefinedTerm.description: Charging a reduced rate for repeated prompt prefixes. Anthropic charges 1.25x base input to write a 5-minute cache and 0.1x to read it (0.025x on Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1), which can cut effective input cost by up to 90%.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Batch API discount
hasDefinedTerm.description: A 50% reduction on both input and output tokens for asynchronous processing, offered by both OpenAI and Anthropic. Applies to distillation-corpus generation, halving the teacher-query bill.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Peak/off-peak pricing
hasDefinedTerm.description: Time-of-day API pricing, introduced by DeepSeek on 16 August 2026. Peak hours (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) cost double the off-peak rate; 17 of 24 hours remain off-peak.

hasDefinedTerm.name: LLMflation
hasDefinedTerm.description: a16z's term for the ~10x-per-year fall in inference cost at a fixed capability level. Epoch AI measures the same phenomenon at 9x-900x per year across six benchmarks, median near 50x.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Breakeven volume
hasDefinedTerm.description: The monthly token volume at which a fixed-cost self-hosted deployment becomes cheaper than a per-token API. Rises as API prices fall, which is why the case for owning inference has weakened even as distillation has got easier.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cost-of-theft asymmetry
hasDefinedTerm.description: The gap between what it costs to create a capability and what it costs to copy it. For frontier LLMs the ratio is roughly 10^3 to 10^5, because behavioural cloning requires only API access and modest fine-tuning compute.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Model extraction attack
hasDefinedTerm.description: Recovering structural parameters of a black-box model through API queries alone. Carlini et al. recovered the full projection matrix of ada and babbage for under $20 and estimated under $2,000 for gpt-3.5-turbo.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Neocloud
hasDefinedTerm.description: A GPU-specialist cloud provider (Together AI, Fireworks, CoreWeave, RunPod, Vast.ai) that undercuts hyperscalers on GPU-hour pricing. H100 on-demand rates run ~$1.73-$4.00/hr at neoclouds vs $4.00-$8.00 at AWS, GCP and Azure.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Student / teacher
hasDefinedTerm.description: In distillation, the small model being trained (student) and the large model whose outputs it learns from (teacher). Financially: the student is the asset you own, the teacher is the line item on your API bill.
